name: SEM moss leaf surface
prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. The supplied image is the texture edit target. Repair its wrapping seams for use as a repeatable game texture. Preserve its microscope look, scale, grey or restrained green palette and overall density. The current edge cuts do not connect when placed in a2x2repeat. All four corners must meet. Use a regular periodic lattice of slender rhomboid moss cells in parallel vertical columns. Precisely repeat the phase of cell-wall positions at opposite edges. Scientific appearance follows this original brief: Seamlessly tileable square texture: the left edge continues into the right edge and the top into the bottom, evenly lit with no vignette, no single dominant feature, no perspective; viewed straight down onto the surface. The dried surface of a moss leaf (Bryum or Sphagnum-like lamina) at about 300 µm across: long narrow rhomboid cells in parallel rows, each cell slightly sunken with raised cell-wall ridges between them, occasional papillae and a few scattered bacteria and fungal spores. The cell rows run vertically in the image.
